messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: KVCACHE_THROTTLE_HIGH - p99 request latency > 2s for the inference runtime. Impact: some hosted customers seeing 502s and timeouts. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. Link: https://redwood-internal/incidents/6555554321
Alex: I’m primary oncall, pinging who’s available for quick handoff if I need to step out in ~30. Primary/Secondary: Alex / Priya.
Sam: I can take short coverage for 20-30m if you need to step away.
Priya: I’m secondary and can take over if it looks like a rollout issue. Suggest we check KV cache thrashing runbook first.
Alex: Good. Quick status: dashboards show cache hit-rate dropped from 96% -> 45% around 11:03 UTC, autoscaler didn’t spin up new inference pods due to pod startup quota. Might be a burst from embeddings job.
Casey: Noted. I’ll look at the autoscaler logs and node pool quotas. If quota is the blocker we can temporarily bump burst capacity policy.
Marta: tagging ops-qa: did any deploy go out around that time?
Sam: No code deploys listed in deploy-bot above timeline. Deploy-bot: no production deploys in last 60m.
Alex: Runbook pointer: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash - quick checklist: 1) confirm hit-rate drop 2) check autoscaler events 3) increase burst capacity / fallback to smaller model variant 4) apply client-side throttle if too many long sequences.
Priya: I’m running these checks. First check: cache hit-rate, confirmed.
Casey: Autoscaler events showing "scale blocked by quota: 4 nodes requested, 0 available". Node pool is at project quota.
Alex: Ok mitigation options: A) enable emergency burst (policy->force-burst) for 10m, B) roll global routing to fallback model small-quantized, C) apply cluster-level throttle via service-mesh rate limit to embeddings-route. Which do we prefer?
Priya: For minimum customer impact do B then A if B doesn't reduce load. Rolling to small-quantized will use less GPU memory and reduce pod creation time.
Sam: I can trigger the model fallback rollout (console->routes->/v1/embeddings->fallback:small-q). Will do a canary to 5% first.
Alex: Make sure to include the safety header so telemetry marks it as fallback: X-Redwood-Fallback: forced-fallback-6555554321.
Sam: Doing canary now. Command I used via CLI: ```rwrctl rollout set --route /v1/embeddings --variant small-quantized --percent 5 --meta "forced-fallback-6555554321"```
IncidentBot: Rollout event: canary 5% applied by Sam at 11:07 UTC.
Priya: Monitoring ingress errors and p99. Early signal: 5% route reduced local pod memory by ~8% per node in canary traffic.
Casey: Meanwhile, I’ve requested quota bump with infra (ticket INF-9223) and also unlocked emergency burst policy for this project. If rollout doesn't stabilize within 5m, enable burst.
Alex: If we enable burst, note the quick command: ```# enable emergency burst for project
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://redwood-internal/api/v1/projects/redwood/force-burst?duration=10m```
Marta: Heads-up: customer-facing alerts page shows a subset of customers with elevated errors. We should prepare a short incident blurb if this extends beyond 15m.
Priya: p99 dropped from 2.3s to 1.1s in canary region 1 within 90s, good sign. Rolling canary to 25% now.
Sam: Rolling to 25%: ```rwrctl rollout set --route /v1/embeddings --variant small-quantized --percent 25 --meta "forced-fallback-6555554321"```
IncidentBot: Rollout event: 25% applied by Sam at 11:09 UTC.
Casey: Infra responded: quota temporary bump approved + node pool refill in progress ETA 5m. If node pool finishes, we can revert rollout back to default model to restore perf/quality.
Alex: Action list so far: Sam -> handle rollout canary and monitor. Priya -> monitor p99, hit-rate. Casey -> node quota / burst unlock. Marta -> prep customer blurb draft. I’ll stay primary unless I need to step out.
Sam: Noted, monitoring logs and will post back at 11:15 with status.
Marta: Draft blurb: "Experiencing elevated inference latency for embeddings for a subset of customers. We are rolling a temporary fallback variant to mitigate while we scale capacity. No data exposure. Monitoring ongoing, updates in 15m." Thoughts?
Alex: Good. Add note about estimated mitigation: "Mitigation in progress; degraded quality expected for fallback variant for ~10-30m" and link to status page.
Priya: Update at 11:12: p99 across global dropped to 1.05s, error rate down 70%. Can keep ramping rollback decision in 10m if node refill completes.
Sam: At 11:14 canary -> 80%, still steady.
Casey: Node pool refill completed at 11:16 (nodes available). I’m safe to revert burst and start reverting to primary variant.
Alex: Ok plan: Sam, start rollback to default model in canary increments 20% -> 50% -> 100% while monitoring p99 and customer errors. Use traffic shaping to minimize churn.
Sam: Rolling back: ```rwrctl rollout set --route /v1/embeddings --variant default-highperf --percent 20 --meta "revert-after-6555554321"```
IncidentBot: Rollout event: revert 20% by Sam at 11:18 UTC.
Priya: Watching: p99 remains ~1.1s during rollback, error rate stable.
Marta: Sending incident blurb to status page and CSE team now. Posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/6555554321
Alex: Quick handoff note in case I step out: Priya is secondary and will be primary if I leave; pager routing remains unchanged. Runbook quick links: KV cache runbook (https://redwood-internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash), Rollout playbook (https://redwood-internal/runbooks/rollouts), Emergency burst policy (https://redwood-internal/policies/burst).
Sam: Reverted to default 100% at 11:22. ```rwrctl rollout set --route /v1/embeddings --variant default-highperf --percent 100 --meta "revert-complete-6555554321"```
IncidentBot: Rollout event: 100% default applied by Sam at 11:22 UTC.
Priya: Final metrics at 11:25: p99 0.95s, error rate baseline restored, cache hit-rate back to 94%.
Alex: Great. Post-incident TODOs: - write short postmortem entry (owner: Alex) - confirm autoscaler quota/instrumentation improvements (owner: Casey) - add automatic fallback variant test in chaos suite (owner: Sam) - update runbook with the exact curl and rwrctl snippets we used (owner: Priya).
Marta: Acknowledged, I’ll coordinate customer comms and CSE follow-ups.
Sam: Thanks all. If Alex needs to step out I’ll step in for immediate followups.
Alex: I need to take a 15min break now, handing primary to Priya. Priya, you’re primary from 11:30 -> 11:45.
Priya: Confirmed taking primary. Leaving handoff note in oncall doc. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: Incident 6555554321 resolved: mitigation complete, monitoring continues.
